state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Remember, the negative-sloping section on the graph represents Fido moving away from his home. How can we use this information to figure out what might have happened during that time?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh wait, so the negative slope means he's moving away? But I thought negative meant going backwards or something bad happening... So if the distance is going down on the graph, that means he's getting closer to home, right? Is that what the negative slope shows?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Remember, the negative slope on the graph actually represents Fido moving away from his home. How does this new understanding change your interpretation of the negative-sloping section?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly states incorrect information (claiming negative slope means moving away from home when it actually means returning home), fails to engage with the student's emerging correct understanding in Turn 2, and provides no scaffolding that would help the student reason through the graph interpretation.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses repetitive scaffolding language but provides incorrect mathematical information (claiming negative slope means moving away when it actually means decreasing distance/returning home), fails to diagnose the student's correct reasoning in Turn 2, and doesn't adjust support based on student progress.
